title: Appendicitis
summary: The supplied search results contain no appendicitis-specific diagnostic, imaging, antibiotic, operative, or nonoperative-management evidence. Consequently, this review identifies the evidence gap rather than extrapolating from unrelated infectious disease guidelines.
seoDescription: Evidence-aware overview of appendicitis noting that the supplied literature does not provide appendicitis-specific diagnostic or management guidance.
clinicalQuestion: What appendicitis-specific diagnostic and management guidance is supported by the supplied literature?
keyTakeaways: No supplied source addresses appendicitis diagnosis, imaging, antibiotics, operative treatment, or outcomes; appendicitis-specific recommendations cannot be supported from this evidence set.
Clinical practice guidelines should be based on systematic evidence review and assessment of benefits and harms of alternative care options.[9]
IDSA distinguishes formal clinical practice guidelines, which use systematic review and GRADE, from clinical guidance documents that may not include formal evidence grading.[10]

sections.heading: Appendicitis evidence is absent from the supplied search results
sections.intro: Do not extrapolate unrelated guidance to appendicitis.
paragraphs: The supplied results primarily address clinical-practice-guideline methodology and COVID-19 therapeutics; one source addresses complicated urinary tract infection. None provides appendicitis-specific evidence for clinical risk stratification, laboratory testing, ultrasound, CT, MRI, antimicrobial selection or dosing, appendectomy, nonoperative management, perforation, abscess, drainage, or follow-up. Therefore, no patient-specific diagnostic or treatment recommendation for appendicitis can be made from these sources.

A trustworthy clinical practice guideline is informed by systematic review of evidence and assessment of benefits and harms of alternative care options.[9] IDSA describes its clinical practice guidelines as systematic-review- and GRADE-based recommendations, whereas its clinical guidance documents may be based on comprehensive review and expert experience without formal evidence grading.[10]
bullets: Obtain a current appendicitis-specific guideline, surgical society statement, radiology appropriateness criteria, and local antimicrobial pathway before using this topic for point-of-care decisions.
Do not use the COVID-19 antiviral, immunomodulator, or prophylaxis recommendations in the supplied results to select therapy for suspected or confirmed appendicitis.[11]

faq.question: Can the supplied sources support an appendicitis treatment algorithm?
faq.answer: No. They contain no appendicitis-specific diagnostic or management data, so an evidence-grounded algorithm, imaging sequence, antibiotic regimen, or operative recommendation cannot be generated.

faq.question: Why not infer appendicitis management from complicated UTI guidance?
faq.answer: The complicated UTI guideline is syndrome-specific and addresses urinary infections, including empiric antibiotic selection, IV-to-oral transition, and treatment duration; it is not evidence for appendicitis.[19]
